scripts.//build: Vercel treats a 200.html at the output root as an SPA fallback and serves it for EVERY unknown path with HTTP 200 — a site-wide soft-404 (Googlebot-Image got HTML back from /favicon.ico, /apple-touch-icon.png and every typo'd URL, all tagged index,follow). The site is fully prerendered and needs no SPA fallback, so the file is dropped and Vercel falls back to the prerendered 404.html, which already sets a real 404 status and noindex,nofollow.
scripts.build: nuxt build && node -e "for(const f of ['200.html','200.html.br','200.html.gz'])require('fs').rmSync('.output/public/'+f,{force:true})" && node scripts/strip-leaked-paths.mjs && node scripts/inline-critical-css.mjs && node scripts/check-seo-assets.mjs

//overrides.esbuild: pinned ahead of the transitive range
//overrides.sharp: @nuxt/image@1.x declares ipx@^2.1.1 as an optionalDependency, and ipx@2.1.1 pins sharp@^0.32.6 — vulnerable libvips (GHSA-f88m-g3jw-g9cj). The upstream fix is @nuxt/image@2, which requires @nuxt/kit@4 (i.e. a Nuxt 3 -> 4 migration). Forcing sharp>=0.35 clears the advisory while staying on Nuxt 3: ipx only calls long-stable sharp APIs (resize/rotate/extract/extend/toFormat/toBuffer). Remove this override when migrating to Nuxt 4 + @nuxt/image@2.
